name: Villa XXII
tagline: A study in light, scale and stillness in Jumeirah Islands.
summary: Villa XXII is a landmark six-bedroom residence, 11,800 sq ft of built-up area on a 14,500 sq ft plot, that opens through black arches and double-height volumes onto a private pool meeting the lake and fairway beyond.
story: Delivered end-to-end to our turnkey standard, the home resolves structure, MEP, bespoke joinery, marble and smart-home automation as one seamless vision, a composed statement of privacy, craft and quiet luxury.

chapters.title: Living, on a double-height scale.
chapters.text: Nearly nine metres of glass and stone rise to a cascading crystal chandelier. A bookmatched marble media wall anchors deep bouclé seating, while floor-to-ceiling glazing dissolves the wall between salon and garden.

chapters.title: A kitchen wrapped in walnut and stone.
chapters.text: Hand-finished walnut joinery and a single slab of stone form a generous island. Full-height glazing draws the green of the fairway directly to the cook's counter, engineered for quiet family mornings and high-level entertaining alike.

chapters.title: Gather, under alabaster light.
chapters.text: A stone-topped table for ten sits beneath twin alabaster pendants, framed by arches that open to the salon on one side and the breakfast kitchen on the other, held in the home's calm palette of stone, walnut and warm gold light.

chapters.title: A grand foyer and a light-filled void.
chapters.text: Three black-framed arches frame the heart of the home, a grand piano resting on a sunburst rug beneath a mirrored ceiling inlay, with the salon reading as one continuous gesture from the mezzanine above.

chapters.title: A quiet altar for the evening.
chapters.text: A fluted, back-lit arch glows within seamless oak, a considered home for crystal, decanters and a private collection. Tactile, warm and made for the close of the evening, with concealed LED washing every shelf.

chapters.title: A wellness suite built in.
chapters.text: A mirror-clad, fully-equipped gym with treatment tables and warm oak surrounds, a back-lit manifesto sets the tone. Designed for daily training and genuine recovery without leaving the residence.

chapters.title: Living, onto the water.
chapters.text: The private pool draws the eye across a still lake to manicured greens. Teak loungers, framed planting and an outdoor shower complete a terrace built for long golden hours against the estate.

chapters.title: On the edge of the water.
chapters.text: A resort-grade pool and landscaped garden run straight out to the lake, the calm of Jumeirah Islands as a private backdrop, framed by a clean contemporary façade of stone and stucco.

name: Villa Arterra
tagline: A beachfront sanctuary on the fronds of Palm Jumeirah.
summary: Villa Arterra is a fully reimagined five-bedroom residence set directly on the beach of Palm Jumeirah, a warm, light-filled home where book-matched marble, oak joinery and brushed-gold ceilings frame uninterrupted views across the water to the Dubai Marina skyline.
story: Delivered turnkey to our standard through a complete structural and interior renovation, the home is shaped around stillness, zen water gardens, a floating stone staircase and floor-to-ceiling glazing that draws the sea and sky into every room.

chapters.title: Warmth, held in stone and gold.
chapters.text: The principal living volume runs the depth of the home beneath a brushed-gold lattice ceiling, anchored by a full-width marble fireplace, opening seamlessly to the kitchen and the sculptural staircase beyond.

chapters.title: One volume, open to the sea.
chapters.text: A generous sectional sits beneath a coffered gold ceiling, with the open kitchen and dining set behind and full-height glazing drawing in the beach and skyline. Travertine, oak and soft neutral upholstery hold the room in a calm, tactile palette.

chapters.title: A quieter room, made for evenings.
chapters.text: An intimate media lounge wrapped in upholstered panelling and oak, with a sculptural floor lamp, leather-trimmed seating and a sliding glass wall opening to the planting outside, a softer counterpoint to the main living space.

chapters.title: A floating stone staircase over a zen garden.
chapters.text: The heart of the home is a double-height void where cantilevered marble treads float above a still water garden and bonsai, circulation reimagined as sculpture, lit by a cascade of hand-formed lighting.

chapters.title: Wake to the skyline and the sea.
chapters.text: The principal bedroom opens through a full corner of glazing onto the beach and the Marina skyline beyond, an onyx-and-oak headboard, fluted walnut walls and a soft neutral palette set against the water.

chapters.title: An entrance staged like a gallery.
chapters.text: A sculpted stone console sits between backlit display vitrines and a travertine feature wall, with the floating staircase rising alongside, the first gesture of a home built around light, stone and calm.

chapters.title: A façade with quiet authority.
chapters.text: A timber-battened carport and a clean contemporary elevation in stone and glass frame the arrival court, a restrained, confident presence on the frond, with mature planting and an integrated lighting line.

name: Villa Serein
tagline: A quiet palace, softly drawn.
summary: Villa Serein sits behind a white plaster façade of tall slender arches and fine black steel glazing, a classical silhouette pared back until only its proportion remains. Inside, the house works in one continuous palette: alabaster plaster, hand-painted botanical panels, honed travertine and pale oak, lifted by olive velvet and antique bronze.
story: Our team delivered the residence end to end, structure, façade, glazing, marble, joinery, decorative finishes, lighting, automation and landscape, so every room of a very large house reads as a single, unhurried idea.

chapters.title: Framed by an arch.
chapters.text: The formal salon is entered through a full-height plaster arch and closes on a black steel window drawn as three slender arches. Bouclé seating, an olive velvet ottoman and a travertine hearth sit on pale oak, soft volumes against hard, exact lines.

chapters.title: Symmetry, held lightly.
chapters.text: A single sculpted stone table sits on axis between two steel doors, under a ribboned crystal pendant. Hand-painted botanical panels line the walls behind sheer linen, and every element, glassware, candlesticks, bronze rings, is placed to the room's centreline.

chapters.title: Three arches, one wall.
chapters.text: Arched oak cabinets, glazed, backlit and fluted between, run the length of a hand-painted landscape mural. A book-matched marble island anchors the room, with a rippled glass light drawn across it like water.

chapters.title: Carved, curved, quiet.
chapters.text: A bas-relief plaster headboard wall curves around the bed, lit from a floating ceiling raft printed with the same botanical hand. Herringbone oak, an olive bench and twisted alabaster pendants keep a very large room intimate.

chapters.title: Where the house turns personal.
chapters.text: Two small rooms carry the most character, a bronze-lined study with a travertine desk and full-height garden window, and a powder room in oxblood plaster, arabescato marble and fluted stone.

chapters.title: Under a star ceiling.
chapters.text: Two tiers of modular oxblood velvet face a full-wall screen, with linear light cut into the panelling and a fibre-optic star field overhead. Acoustics, lighting scenes and AV were coordinated in-house with the joinery so nothing is applied after the fact.

chapters.title: A wing for the end of the day.
chapters.text: A mirrored gym opens to a planted light well; beyond it, a sculpted micro-cement spa with a raised jacuzzi, sunken plunge pool and a second star ceiling.

name: La Mer Villa
tagline: Stacked slabs, softened corners.
summary: La Mer Villa is organised as three travertine trays with radiused edges, each one planted along its lip so the house reads as terraces of greenery rather than storeys. Bronze, carport, pergola, gates, screens, is the only other exterior material.
story: Inside, the same restraint holds: travertine and warm oak on every plane, green marble as the recurring accent, and cognac leather for the furniture. A floating stone stair and a double-height reception tie the ground floor together.

chapters.title: The house opens to the water.
chapters.text: The whole ground floor slides open onto one terrace: lounge, dining and outdoor kitchen under the slab, a green mosaic pool with a sunken deck, and an olive tree set into the paving as the pivot between them.

chapters.title: Closed to the street, open to the garden.
chapters.text: A bronze-clad boundary with fluted gates gives the street front total privacy; on the garden side the same slabs open into full-height glazing, balconies and the pool.

chapters.title: A bronze wing, lit from within.
chapters.text: The carport is a single folded bronze plane on slim paired columns, its underside lined with timber battens and two continuous light slots. Planters and self-watering troughs run along both edges so the structure sits in green from every approach.

chapters.title: Boucle, cognac, one curved line.
chapters.text: Two long boucle sofas and a pair of cognac leather swivels sit on a sand rug drawn with a single wandering line, under a rounded cove-lit ceiling ring that repeats the plan of the room. Sheer curtains run the full height of the glazing.

chapters.title: Green marble, book-matched.
chapters.text: The family sitting room centres on a leather-wrapped media panel flanked by full-height book-matched green marble, with a linear fire below and a slim bronze light grazing the joint. Travertine returns and glass-shelved joinery close the room on the other side.

chapters.title: Eight seats, under the stair.
chapters.text: The dining table sits directly against the floating stair, so the treads become the backdrop. Lit marble display joinery runs the opposite wall, and a linear crossed pendant in ribbed glass hangs low over the setting.

chapters.title: Two pieces of pure stonework.
chapters.text: The cantilevered stair and the show kitchen island were both set out slab by slab, every tread and every mitre matched to the vein before anything was cut.

chapters.title: Two hundred bottles, backlit.
chapters.text: A single brass grid holds the collection against a backlit onyx wall, turning storage into the light source for the room. Blackened joinery with lit shelves, a stone counter and a chilled cabinet handle the service side.

chapters.title: Glazed, so it stays on view.
chapters.text: The cellar sits behind a black steel and glass screen, lighting the lounge in front of it. Curved boucle sofas, an oxblood armchair, olive recliners and a green marble drum table gather on a chevron rug under a crossed bronze pendant.

chapters.title: Quieter, not simpler.
chapters.text: Bedrooms and the study keep the same joinery discipline, fluted panels, oak, stone niches, with the palette pulled back to a single tone per room.

chapters.title: The service floor, finished like the rest.
chapters.text: Gym and garage are treated as rooms, not utilities: full-height oak panelling, integrated equipment joinery, batten ceilings and concealed linear light.

name: Vista Luxe
tagline: Turnkey luxury, reimagined on the Palm.
summary: Vista Luxe is a fully turnkey residence on Palm Jumeirah, a masterclass in our structural execution, where the original grand-foyer layout was reimagined and expanded from 5,000 to 6,100 sq ft of built-up area.
story: A showcase for high-performance architectural design, the home blends signature modern innovation with a timeless material palette, bespoke finishes and bold contemporary accents set against a panoramic horizon framing the Burj Al Arab and the Dubai Marina skyline.

chapters.title: Living and dining, in one open volume.
chapters.text: A single flowing social zone runs from a sculptural dining table through to a curved lounge and backlit display walls, herringbone oak floors, halo-lit ceiling coves and wide cased arches holding the whole expanse in a calm, tonal palette.

chapters.title: A kitchen framed by sculpted arches.
chapters.text: Twin oak arches open onto a fluted island in stone and brushed metal, with integrated appliances and a concealed back kitchen behind. Warm timber, dark cabinetry and gold detailing balance everyday family life with high-level entertaining.

chapters.title: A staircase that draws the light down.
chapters.text: The reimagined foyer rises through a sculptural double-height void, a floating stair edged in concealed light, micro-cement walls and a circular skylight that pulls daylight to the heart of the home.

chapters.title: A spa retreat in stone and oak.
chapters.text: A freestanding sculpted tub sits beneath bespoke oak cabinetry, with a marble-clad walk-in shower framed by a dramatic book-matched arch, black fittings and warm timber against soft micro-cement walls.

chapters.title: A private study, wrapped in warmth.
chapters.text: A serene workspace anchored by a halo-lit circular cove and a backlit oak media wall, with arched windows draped in full-height sheers. A sculpted desk and curved sofa make a room engineered equally for focus and quiet retreat.

chapters.title: Living, onto the sea.
chapters.text: A sprawling pool, sunken fire-pit lounge and fully equipped barbecue and dining zone open straight onto the beach, one of the largest Garden Home plots on the Palm, framed by curated, lush landscaping and the lights of Dubai beyond.

chapters.title: A clean line against the coastline.
chapters.text: From a crisp contemporary façade to the pool deck and beach, Vista Luxe reads as a single confident gesture, a structurally expanded residence holding the full sweep of Palm Jumeirah as its private backdrop.

name: Villa 27, Sienna Lakes
tagline: Golf-course living, on the edge of Sienna Lakes.
summary: Fully transformed by our team, this golf course-facing Sienna Lakes villa in Jumeirah Golf Estates blends Mediterranean charm with sleek, contemporary sophistication, roughly 7,200 sq ft behind oversized arched windows and a stone-clad tower.
story: Five en-suite bedrooms, a dedicated home office, a striking double-height living room, a basement cinema and a designer kitchen and bar, the premium finishes extending outdoors to a landscaped garden, pool and lounge, all overlooking spectacular golf-course views.

chapters.title: Living, on a double-height scale.
chapters.text: The main living volume rises through two storeys to a cascade of porcelain-petal pendants, anchored by a green-marble fireplace wall, oak media joinery and oversized glazing that pulls the golf-course greenery indoors.

chapters.title: A wardrobe carved in warm oak.
chapters.text: A walk-in dressing room runs floor-to-ceiling in fumed oak, backlit display niches, integrated hanging and a herringbone floor, every shelf and drawer crafted in-house to a seamless, hotel-grade standard.

chapters.title: Bathe with the fairway in view.
chapters.text: A sculpted freestanding tub sits to a full-height window over the garden and golf course, micro-cement walls, a backlit round mirror and a textured stone feature wall in a calm, light-filled retreat.

chapters.title: Bedrooms with character and play.
chapters.text: The children's suites pair built-in bunk joinery and integrated lighting with playful safari art, bouclé beanbags and soft olive-green accents, bespoke, characterful rooms that still hold the home's quiet, tonal palette.

chapters.title: A stone tower, lit against the night.
chapters.text: After dark, integrated façade lighting traces the villa's Mediterranean geometry, the stone-clad tower, the oversized arched windows and the warm glow of the double-height living room beyond.

name: Marina Residence
tagline: A duplex built around the light.
summary: Thirteen thousand square feet on two floors at the head of Marina Residence 1, with the marina on one side and the open Gulf on the other. The plan gives everything to the view: a double-height salon under a full glass wall, a floating mezzanine above it, and every reception room drawn back so the horizon reaches the middle of the home.
story: Our team delivered the residence end to end, full strip-out, layout reconfiguration, marble, oak joinery, lighting, automation and styling, a single palette of grey-veined stone, rift oak and warm linen carried through all six bedrooms and the rooftop terrace.

chapters.title: Two floors of daylight.
chapters.text: The main volume runs the full height of the duplex. Rift-oak panelling and slender book-matched stone piers rise unbroken to the mezzanine, and a cluster of hand-formed mesh pendants hangs in the centre of the space so the room reads as one room, not two floors.

chapters.title: Four settings, one room.
chapters.text: Low linen seating is arranged in loose groups across a single stone floor, a long sofa to the glass, a facing pair, a daybed on axis, so the salon holds a quiet evening for two or a full gathering without being rearranged. The enfilade runs straight through to the dining room and kitchen beyond.

chapters.title: One slab, ten seats.
chapters.text: A single grey-and-amber marble slab makes the dining table, repeated in the island and the lit backsplash niche behind it. An alabaster linear chandelier holds the axis; the working kitchen sits behind full-height oak doors so the room never looks like a kitchen when it isn't one.

chapters.title: Behind the mashrabiya.
chapters.text: The principal suite occupies its own wing, with a sitting room, media wall and bed all facing an arched window screened in fretwork. Herringbone oak, a book-matched stone headboard wall and slim vertical alabaster sconces keep a very wide room composed and symmetrical.

chapters.title: Six suites, one language.
chapters.text: Every bedroom is finished in the same oak, plaster and stone as the reception floor, fluted panelling, concealed cove light and a marble ledge instead of a bedside table, with a full travertine bathroom to each.

chapters.title: Sunset, through three arches.
chapters.text: The roof level keeps the building's stone arcade and fills it with an outdoor kitchen, bar seating and a long dining table. Planting softens the parapet, uplights wash the columns after dark, and the whole terrace faces west over the Palm to the skyline.

chapters.title: The parts nobody photographs.
chapters.text: A sculpted bronze-and-glass stair links the two floors past a lit stone niche; off the private landing, a fully fitted beauty room in rift oak with a wash basin, mirror and chevron floor.

chapters.title: Entered on axis.
chapters.text: From the private lift the home opens on a travertine gallery of deep portals, with the salon to one side and the lit stone stair rising to the mezzanine ahead, the first view is straight through the house to the water.

name: Bluewaters Apartment
tagline: Island living, reimagined for the discerning buyer.
summary: A stunning 2,474 sq ft apartment in Building 1 at Bluewaters Residences, comprehensively reimagined by our team into a premium, turnkey luxury home, contemporary architectural lines paired with high-end finishes throughout.
story: Four elegant bedrooms, a gourmet kitchen integrated with an expansive open-plan living area, a private master sanctuary with bespoke cabinetry and an independent maid's quarter, interiors that flow onto a massive terrace with unobstructed, panoramic vistas of the Arabian Gulf.

chapters.title: Living, opened to the sea.
chapters.text: A single open volume runs from a sculptural modular sofa to the dining and kitchen beyond, book-matched marble floors, warm timber accents and a hand-carved sculpture set against a wall of glass and the turquoise Gulf.

chapters.title: A gourmet kitchen, wrapped in marble.
chapters.text: A book-matched marble island anchors the kitchen, framed by handleless cabinetry, glazed display joinery and integrated appliances. An oak dining table sits to the glazing, golf-grade entertaining with the sea as a backdrop.

chapters.title: A media wall in oak and stone.
chapters.text: A bespoke oak media wall, crowned by a backlit marble panel and flanked by lit display niches, anchors the second lounge, a calm, tactile composition of timber, stone and curated sculpture against the sea light.

chapters.title: A bedroom that wakes to the Gulf.
chapters.text: The private master sanctuary is pared back and serene, a woven-leather bed, full-height sea glazing and a study nook to the view, with bespoke floor-to-ceiling cabinetry keeping the space calm and uncluttered.

chapters.title: A jewel box in stone and shadow.
chapters.text: Deep micro-cement walls wrap a carved-marble vessel basin, an organic backlit mirror and an onyx display niche, a moody, tactile counterpoint to the bright, sea-washed living spaces.

name: Cayan Duplex
tagline: Two levels, one quiet line.
summary: A duplex in Cayan Tower, Dubai Marina. The brief was calm, pared-back luxury: oak, travertine and soft grey velvet, with the Marina framed by full-height windows.
story: A floating oak staircase with a frameless glass balustrade links the two levels, rising through a double-height lounge. Flush oak wall panels hide storage and doors, while lit niches and a glazed wine wall add warmth after dark.

chapters.title: One open floor, wrapped in oak.
chapters.text: The lounge, dining table and kitchen share a single open plan, held together by a continuous oak wall with lit niches and a glazed wine store. Paper-leaf pendants float over the sofa, with the staircase rising behind.

chapters.title: Travertine, oak and a table that flows.
chapters.text: A travertine island runs straight into a curved oak dining table on a brushed brass column, seating six on velvet chairs. Handleless cabinetry, a lit travertine splashback and integrated appliances keep the kitchen quiet.

chapters.title: Soft grey velvet, floating light.
chapters.text: A low modular velvet sofa and a sculpted black coffee table sit beneath three paper-leaf pendants and a cove-lit ceiling, looking through to the kitchen and its oak and travertine wall.

chapters.title: Arriving to the Marina.
chapters.text: The entrance runs along a wall of flush oak panels with a concealed door, opening onto the double-height living space. The floating stair climbs to the gallery above, with the Marina towers filling the full-height windows.

chapters.title: Calm, by design.
chapters.text: A full-width channel-tufted headboard with a hidden light line sits against a soft plaster wall, flanked by floating oak bedside units and slim glass pendants. Tall wardrobes with timber pulls line the walk through.

name: Villa Quindici
tagline: Calm lines, warm materials.
summary: Villa Quindici is a family villa in Sienna Lakes. Its street façade pairs a stone-clad entrance tower and a tall timber-slatted door with the community’s terracotta roofs, while the garden side opens onto a pool, a covered roof terrace and full-height sliding glass.
story: Inside, the palette is calm and tailored: grey marble floors and stairs, dark timber panelling with fine metal inlays, slatted walnut screens and soft linen-toned walls. A lower level is given over to entertaining, with a wine bar in deep red marble, a music lounge and a gallery-style garage.

chapters.title: Pool, terrace and open glass.
chapters.text: At the back, three sets of full-height sliding doors open the ground floor onto a pool and lounge terrace. Above, a covered roof terrace runs the width of the villa under a slatted timber pergola, lit at night by warm wall lights.

chapters.title: A staircase lit from below.
chapters.text: The entrance hall is built around a floating staircase in grey marble, each tread washed with concealed light and edged with a glass balustrade. Dark timber panelling with fine metal inlays sets off the stone and the owner’s art.

chapters.title: Fire, linen and timber.
chapters.text: The family room centres on a media wall in textured linen and dark timber, with lit open shelving and a linear fireplace set into stone. Slatted timber columns and a long built-in sofa frame the space, with the garden beyond.

chapters.title: A table for ten.
chapters.text: A dark marble table seats ten under sculptural linear pendants, between the living room and full-height glazing to the garden. A tall column in textured timber anchors the room and hides the structure behind it.

chapters.title: Screened in walnut.
chapters.text: A freestanding wall of slatted walnut stands behind the bed, screening the walk-in wardrobe while letting light through. Floor-to-ceiling windows, a channelled upholstered headboard and full-height fabric-panelled wardrobes keep the room calm.

chapters.title: Bronze glass, soft light.
chapters.text: Behind the screen, the dressing room is lined with bronze-framed glass wardrobes, each lit inside, facing a long timber vanity and a suspended round mirror. Dark oak floors run through from the bedroom.

chapters.title: A wine bar and a music lounge.
chapters.text: The lower level is made for evenings: a wine bar in deep red marble with backlit display shelving and climate-controlled wine fridges, opening onto a lounge with a lit domed ceiling, curved velvet chairs and a wall of framed records.

name: Villa Aurelia
tagline: A classical villa, brought back to light.
summary: Villa Aurelia is a family home in Jumeirah Islands, renovated end-to-end by our team. Outside, the facade was refined with crisp classical mouldings, tall black-framed glazing and a grand arched window. The garden was rebuilt around a new pool, a sunken fire lounge and a pergola kitchen.
story: Inside, a palette of travertine, oak herringbone, olive velvet and cognac leather runs through a double-height lounge, an open kitchen framed by bronze-trimmed arches, a formal dining room and calm, tailored bedrooms.

chapters.title: Travertine, velvet and afternoon light.
chapters.text: A curved olive velvet sofa and cognac leather armchairs gather around marble coffee tables, beneath a sculptural bronze chandelier. Behind them, a travertine stair rises through the double-height space to a timber-lined gallery.

chapters.title: Rooms joined by bronze arches.
chapters.text: Bronze-trimmed arches frame the view from the family lounge into the kitchen, where a book-matched marble island sits under fluted glass cabinets. The stair treads are lit from below and finished in the same stone.

chapters.title: A table for long evenings.
chapters.text: An oval marble table seats guests between cognac leather chairs and a tufted olive banquette topped with planting. Woven brass pendants hang from a lit ceiling coffer, with full-height oak joinery and glazed display cabinets on either side.

chapters.title: Leather, oak and stone.
chapters.text: A wide leather headboard wall anchors the master suite, set against oak panelling with lit reveals and a backlit marble slab. A pair of velvet lounge chairs creates a quiet reading corner by the window.

chapters.title: A pool that holds the evening.
chapters.text: The rebuilt garden centres on a mosaic-lined pool with a connected spa pool and a sunken lounge around a fire pit, set just below the water line. Uplit palms and layered tropical planting frame it all, with loungers on a timber deck.

chapters.title: A softer, playful note.
chapters.text: A scalloped linen headboard in soft blue runs the width of the wall, framed by classical panelling, glass pendant lights and curved oak bedside tables. Built-in shelving and a study desk complete the room.

name: Fairmont Apartment
tagline: Warm, quiet luxury, on the Palm.
summary: An apartment at Fairmont The Palm. The brief was a calm, contemporary home: a soft palette of sand, oak and stone, lit by architectural track lighting and warmed by afternoon sun off the Gulf.
story: Herringbone oak floors run through every room. Bespoke joinery, marble surfaces and integrated lighting tie the living, dining and bedroom spaces into one considered whole, with the terrace and Dubai skyline always in view.

chapters.title: Soft forms, city light.
chapters.text: A curved bouclé sofa and armchair face a floating oak media wall, while sheer curtains filter the light from full-height windows onto the Dubai skyline. Lit shelving turns a quiet corner into a reading nook.

chapters.title: A table set in stone and walnut.
chapters.text: A veined marble dining table is framed by walnut-armed chairs, with a sculptural pendant above. Behind it, backlit floating shelves and a stone-lined bar niche turn the wall into a display.

chapters.title: A stone wall, opening to the terrace.
chapters.text: A dramatic veined-marble media wall sits beside tall, lit glass cabinets, with a low oak plinth running beneath. Sliding doors open onto the arched terrace and its outdoor dining table.

chapters.title: Layered textures, made for rest.
chapters.text: A channel-tufted headboard sits against a dark glass panel, framed by soft fabric walls and slim pendant lights. Oak bedside tables and an upholstered bench complete a calm, hotel-grade suite.

chapters.title: A ring of light, in the suite.
chapters.text: A bespoke vanity in oak and marble sits beneath a backlit circular mirror, with drawers and a dressing stool built into the same line of joinery as the bedroom.

name: Balqis Penthouse
tagline: Classical calm, island light.
summary: A full-floor penthouse at Balqis Residence, Palm Jumeirah, conceived as a quiet, contemporary interpretation of classical interiors, soft panelled walls, arched thresholds and herringbone oak, held together by a palette of bone, taupe, olive and oxblood.
story: Our team delivered the residence end to end: joinery, marble, glazing, lighting, automation and styling, with an entertaining sequence that runs from the show kitchen and cinema through to the games room and the terrace above the island.

chapters.title: One slab, one gesture.
chapters.text: A single book-matched viola panel carries the screen, set into a moulded white surround and flanked by backlit oak display bays. Everything around it stays deliberately quiet, bone upholstery, olive and oxblood accents, a black glass table on herringbone oak.

chapters.title: Cook, pour, gather.
chapters.text: The show kitchen pairs a full calacatta run with a marble breakfast island on cylindrical oak legs, a mirrored bar with suspended stemware and a constellation of smoked-glass pendants. Bronze-framed reeded doors close it off from the formal side of the floor when service needs to disappear.

chapters.title: Leather, stone, low light.
chapters.text: A stone-topped desk on sculpted oak drums sits before library bays lined in oxblood leather and lit shelf by shelf. A slim linear pendant and a picture light do the rest, a room that reads as a private office and a collector's room at once.

chapters.title: The detail you walk through.
chapters.text: Arrival sets the grammar of the whole residence, nested radiused arches, alabaster sconces, marble inlay underfoot, and the principal bathroom answers it with the boldest stone on the floor.

chapters.title: A room that exhales.
chapters.text: Behind an arched oak portal, the principal bedroom keeps to bone panelling, a fluted oak headboard wall with integrated reading lights, and one olive velvet bench at the foot of the bed. The dressing room next door is its opposite: reeded glass, curved oak drawers and a single deep-brown velvet island seat.

chapters.title: Dark walnut, deep velvet.
chapters.text: Two tiers of olive velvet seating face a full-width screen wall, wrapped in acoustically detailed walnut panelling under a coffered ceiling of backlit stone. Side tables, brass reading lamps and carpet chosen to swallow sound complete a room built for the evening.

chapters.title: The other half of the floor.
chapters.text: A games room and a live teppanyaki counter share a lighter language, mosaic terrazzo floors, latticed screens and glazed green tile, so the entertaining wing feels like a change of air rather than more of the same.

chapters.title: Train, then disappear.
chapters.text: The private gym is finished like a room rather than a facility, oak-framed storage bays, lit shelving for weights and balls, a reformer on stone floors and full-height linen curtains that close the whole wall when the session is over.

name: The Steakhouse
tagline: A grill room where the fire is the host.
summary: A steakhouse and cocktail bar in Erbil, planned around an open kitchen that faces the room. Exposed brick, blackened steel and a wood-fired oven set the temperature; hand-patterned cement tile carves service routes out of the polished concrete floor.
story: The material story is deliberately narrow, fluted copper, dark bronze, tan leather and antiqued mirror, carried from the grill counter through the bar and into washrooms finished in green and rosso marble.

chapters.title: Copper, glass, and live flame.
chapters.text: The kitchen reads as one long copper-fluted counter under a blackened steel portal, with antiqued mirror above and the oven's mouth glowing at its centre. Brass heat lamps drop over the pass; a lit condiment bay to the side keeps service off the counter and out of view.

chapters.title: Close enough to hear the grill.
chapters.text: Banquettes sit within a few metres of the pass, separated only by the counter's curved copper nose and a step of cement tile. A cast bull's head on the brick pier and a perforated bronze door detail give the guest side something to read while they wait.

chapters.title: A hearth, not an appliance.
chapters.text: The oven is wrapped in vertical terracotta tile that curves with its drum, its arched mouth framed in blackened steel and set deliberately at eye height from the dining room. Around it the kitchen stays neutral stone, so the fire is the only warm thing in frame.

chapters.title: After dark, the room changes key.
chapters.text: A long bronze bar runs the length of the lounge under a field of disc pendants, its backbar shifting from antiqued mirror tile to a lit grid of cast bull-motif panels, the project's emblem, repeated fifty times over.

chapters.title: The floor does the signposting.
chapters.text: A patterned cement-tile runner is inlaid into the concrete along the full bar frontage, edged in a brass trim that doubles as the kick line. Behind the counter, a perforated bronze drainer strip and mirrored glass-storage bays keep the working side as considered as the guest side.

chapters.title: Low light, high polish.
chapters.text: Panelled bronze columns and a lacquered dark ceiling drop the light level right down, leaving the disc pendants and lit shelving to do the work. Tan leather chairs are the only warm note against the graphite palette.

chapters.title: Two marbles, one arch.
chapters.text: The washrooms take the boldest stone in the project, verde for the male side, rosso for the female, unified by the same illuminated arched mirror and a basketweave marble floor.

chapters.title: One detail, repeated in two keys.
chapters.text: A brushed-brass illuminated arch is the single element both washrooms share, three across the verde vanity, two over the rosso. Everything else changes: tile colour, marble, the direction of the basketweave. The result reads as one design idea rather than two rooms.

name: Villa Solaria
tagline: Classical architecture, recast in contemporary luxury.
summary: Villa Solaria is a grand six-bedroom mansion in the gated community of Jumeirah Islands, a neoclassical envelope of arched windows and ornate mouldings, recast inside as a dramatic, light-filled home built around a double-height salon.
story: Delivered turnkey to our standard, the interior pairs Calacatta Viola marble, walnut joinery and bronze-tinted glass with deep burgundy accents, a confident, glamorous palette executed to the finest tolerances across every trade.

chapters.title: A great room that rises two storeys.
chapters.text: The principal living volume opens to a bronze-glass mezzanine above, anchored by a Calacatta Viola media wall set between fluted oak and marble columns, classical proportion held in a thoroughly contemporary material palette.

chapters.title: Living that flows into the kitchen.
chapters.text: The family living space opens through a sculpted arch to the marble kitchen and breakfast bar, with deep burgundy seating drawing the eye across one continuous, light-filled volume, built for both quiet family life and entertaining at scale.

chapters.title: A kitchen built around a single block of stone.
chapters.text: A waterfall island in book-matched Calacatta Viola anchors the kitchen, wrapped in walnut joinery and lit by arcing brass pendants, a full suite of integrated appliances concealed behind a calm, tailored façade.

chapters.title: A table that seats the whole family.
chapters.text: A sculpted oval dining table in dramatic veined marble sits beneath sculptural lighting, framed by velvet tub chairs and a classical archway opening through to the lounge, formal entertaining in the home's signature stone-and-burgundy palette.

chapters.title: A sculptural staircase beneath a cascade of light.
chapters.text: Circulation is staged as theatre, a cantilevered staircase in bronze-tinted glass and marble rises through the double-height void, beneath a hand-formed copper-and-glass chandelier that falls the full height of the salon.

chapters.title: A suite framed in moulding and marble.
chapters.text: The principal bedroom is wrapped in hand-detailed neoclassical panelling, with a Calacatta Viola media wall, a fluted upholstered headboard and herringbone oak floors, a calm, generous retreat dressed in the home's restrained palette.

chapters.title: A garden made for long Dubai evenings.
chapters.text: A resort-grade pool, a shaded pergola lounge and an outdoor shower sit within mature, fully landscaped grounds, private outdoor living wrapped in established trees and clean stone paving.

name: Villa Octavia
tagline: Classical bones, a modern heart.
summary: Villa Octavia keeps the tiled roofline, carved plaster and arches of a Mediterranean villa in Jumeirah Islands, then opens the interior into a calm, contemporary home of travertine, fumed oak and warm light. The two languages meet at a double-height living core where a suspended emerald-glass installation falls past a full arched window to the pool.
story: Our team delivered the project end to end, structure, glazing, marble, joinery, lighting, automation and landscape, so the heritage façade and the modern interior read as one considered whole.

chapters.title: An emerald cascade.
chapters.text: The heart of the house rises two full storeys to a bespoke installation of hand-cast emerald and clear glass, suspended on fine cables that pour down past an arched window to the garden. Travertine walls, herringbone oak and a honed-stone fireplace hold the room in warm, gallery-quiet calm.

chapters.title: Open, layered, connected.
chapters.text: Beyond the core, a sequence of living spaces unfolds along herringbone oak, a sunken lounge under a coffered ceiling, lit display joinery, a sculptural arch-leg console and a curved black-steel stair. Soft greys, bronze and a circular mirror keep the volume generous and serene.

chapters.title: Dark oak, low light.
chapters.text: A tasting room wrapped in fumed-oak joinery and glazed, climate-controlled cabinets sits off the kitchen behind a slim black-steel arch. Backlit shelving, a chequerboard-marble threshold and a round ebonised table make it a quiet, considered pause between the formal and family wings.

chapters.title: A villa for the open air.
chapters.text: Outside, the house is staged for the evening, a sunken travertine lounge and fire pit between the palms, a lit pool against the arched glazing, and a carved-plaster entrance court that frames the heritage façade.

name: Maison Baroque
tagline: Baroque grandeur, through a lens of contemporary precision.
summary: A our team-executed residence in Cluster 6, Jumeirah Islands, a masterclass that blends Baroque and classical elements with modern flair. The experience begins at a grand mosaic-marble entrance, establishing a structural narrative of refinement carried through the home by natural stone and electroplated-metal accents.
story: Inside, the design challenges convention with high-concept features, a library and cigar lounge crowned by an aluminium bubble ceiling, bespoke in-house joinery and integrated, hidden lighting, every element synchronised to deliver quiet luxury and effortless beauty.

chapters.title: Arrival, beneath a cascade of light.
chapters.text: A double-height hall is anchored by a sculptural floating staircase in dark oak and glass, risers traced in concealed light, a polished-steel sculpture standing sentinel beneath a rain of suspended linear pendants.

chapters.title: A light-filled living, in soft curves.
chapters.text: The main living volume runs full-height to the glazing, anchored by a book-matched marble media wall and a sculptural curved sofa. Caramel-leather lounge chairs and a calm, tonal palette balance the drama of the cascading chandelier above.

chapters.title: Dining, under a flight of amber glass.
chapters.text: A steel-and-glass table is framed by twin marble-backed display walls and a sculptural amber-glass installation overhead, a formal room held in the home's palette of stone, brushed metal and warm light.

chapters.title: A kitchen carved from a single stone.
chapters.text: A monolithic book-matched marble island anchors the room, wrapped in fluted cabinetry, integrated appliances and twin black cylinder hoods. A glazed display column and amber-glass pendant cluster lift the space into the realm of theatre.

chapters.title: Repose, beneath the stair.
chapters.text: A sculptural curved sofa nestles beneath the mirror-clad underside of the floating staircase, bronze-and-glass tables, a cascade of pendants overhead, and reflective surfaces that fold the double-height volume back on itself.

chapters.title: A garden that frames the skyline.
chapters.text: The garden serves as an artful retreat, curated sculptures, a turquoise-tiled pool, a sunken fire-pit lounge and a functional barbecue area, every element synchronised against panoramic views of the Dubai skyline beyond the water.

name: Serenia Residence
tagline: A beachfront apartment, quiet enough to hear the sea.
summary: Serenia Living sits on the west shoulder of Palm Jumeirah, where the glazing faces open water rather than another tower. That single fact set the brief: the interior should never compete with what is outside it.
story: So the palette is short, travertine underfoot, oiled oak and linen on the walls, dark stone and bronze used sparingly. The reception volume runs uninterrupted from the piano through living to dining, with a suspended glass installation the only gesture allowed to raise its voice. Four bedrooms move progressively warmer and darker as you go inward, away from the light.

chapters.title: You enter, and the sea is already there.
chapters.text: The entrance holds back deliberately, a lower timber ceiling, oak and linen panels, dark marble slips lit from within. Past the piano the ceiling lifts and a single framed aperture releases the whole view. Compression, then release: the oldest device in interior architecture, and still the most effective.

chapters.title: A room with no back wall.
chapters.text: Glazing on two sides leaves nowhere to anchor a sofa, so the seating floats, a low modular sectional set on a travertine field, bronze-and-timber lounge chairs turned to the water, occasional tables in dark solid oak. Everything is kept below sill height. Nothing interrupts the horizon line.

chapters.title: Ten seats under falling water.
chapters.text: A single dark-stained ash table, ten upholstered chairs in blush leather and linen, and above it a suspended glass installation that reads as water caught mid-movement. It is the one extravagance in the apartment, and it earns its place by being the only one.

chapters.title: A wall built as a headboard.
chapters.text: The whole rear elevation is joinery: oiled oak in vertical bays, linen-wrapped upper panels, a shadow gap lit from behind, and a curved return that carries the panelling around the corner without a visible joint. Sequenced from one flitch, measured on site after the substrate, which is the only way the grain runs true across nine metres.

chapters.title: Dark stone, warm timber, one soft edge.
chapters.text: Opposite the bed, a floating vanity in dark marble and blackened oak runs the length of the wall, its drawers set on a recessed plinth so the mass appears to hover. The organic backlit mirror is the only curve in the room, placed to catch the sea in reflection from the bed.

chapters.title: The palette, turned all the way down.
chapters.text: Pale oak bays, an ivory upholstered headboard set into a recessed frame, a fluted bench at the foot of the bed and travertine running through from the reception rooms. Bronze pendants drop on slender stems in place of bedside lamps, leaving the tables clear. Almost nothing in the room, and nothing missing from it.

chapters.title: One room allowed a little formality.
chapters.text: The second bedroom takes a classical turn, hand-run wall panelling, a marble dressing ledge running wall to wall, a backlit mirror between bronze sconces, and a slab of book-matched marble at the ensuite threshold. Ivory throughout, so the ornament reads as relief rather than decoration.

name: Victory Heights Villa
tagline: A family villa that holds its warmth.
summary: A full villa interior at Victory Heights, planned around a single open volume where kitchen, dining and living flow into one another. Herringbone oak floors, plaster ceilings and softly arched thresholds give the ground floor a continuous, unhurried rhythm.
story: The palette stays deliberately warm, oak, calacatta, plaster and tan leather, with a printed olive green used as the one recurring accent, from the living-room armchairs to the kitchen stools and the library reading chairs.

chapters.title: A circle, not a row.
chapters.text: Seating is arranged as a conversation circle rather than a wall of furniture: a curved tan sofa, two printed olive armchairs and a stone coffee table, all held on a round wool rug. A paper pendant and a linear plaster fitting keep the ceiling as quiet as the floor is warm.

chapters.title: Ten seats, one gesture overhead.
chapters.text: A marble-topped table on brushed metal drums seats ten, lit by a sculptural jointed plaster pendant that traces the length of the room. Arched niches behind it hold the bar and the pantry, so service stays close but never on show.

chapters.title: Calacatta, oak, and a lit reveal.
chapters.text: A full-height calacatta splash runs behind fluted oak joinery, with backlit reeded-glass cabinets above and a marble island whose slatted oak base is lit from within, the detail that makes the room read at night.

chapters.title: Read here, play there.
chapters.text: A floor-to-ceiling oak bookcase, lit shelf by shelf and backed in marble, faces two green velvet chairs and an upright piano in the corner. Sculpted rugs layer over the herringbone to mark the reading zone without a single wall.

chapters.title: The parts you pass every day.
chapters.text: Thresholds get the same attention as the rooms: a grasscloth-lined seating nook at the entrance, and a marble-inlay floor that curves around the stair to the first-floor lobby.

chapters.title: A suite with its own sitting room.
chapters.text: The principal suite opens onto its own lounge: a lit oak display wall with fine studded reveals, a curved sofa and bench facing the glazing, and a coffered ceiling trimmed in solid timber to bring the volume down to a comfortable height.

chapters.title: Two beds, one piece of joinery.
chapters.text: The double children's room is built around a single bespoke unit: stacked bunks with upholstered headboard panels, integrated cove lighting, a stepped drawer stair and a long shared desk with lit shelving above, storage, sleep and study resolved in one move.

name: Villa Capri
tagline: Classical discipline, modern clarity.
summary: Villa Capri occupies a corner plot in Cluster 28 on Jumeirah Islands, reworked inside and out as a restrained classical house, carved friezes, arched fenestration and a domed centrepiece outside; ivory panelling, herringbone oak and calacatta within.
story: Colour is held to almost nothing: bone, ivory, warm oak and a single dark accent, black marble, ebonised timber, a chocolate velvet cushion, repeated in every room so the whole house reads in one voice.

chapters.title: Ivory, to the ceiling.
chapters.text: Panelling runs the full double height, framing a marble mantel with the screen set flush above it. Three cream sofas face the fire in a closed square, flanked by ebonised side tables and lamps, under a crystal-petal chandelier that fills the upper volume.

chapters.title: One line, three rooms.
chapters.text: A moulded opening lines the second sitting room up with the dining room and the kitchen wall beyond, so a single sightline carries the whole ground floor. Herringbone oak runs unbroken through it, and a bordered rug marks each zone without a door or a step.

chapters.title: Two tables, two kinds of evening.
chapters.text: The formal dining room seats eight at a black stone table under a linear crystal fitting; next door, a round table for six sits between mirrored bar joinery and twin glazed wine columns for the later half of the night.

chapters.title: Oak, leather, low lamplight.
chapters.text: The one room that goes warm: full-height oak library bays lit shelf by shelf, a panelled desk with a marble ledge, a tan Chesterfield facing a round marble table, and a buttoned ottoman on a bordered rug. A slim bronze pendant hangs off-centre over the desk.

chapters.title: Blossom, hand-drawn.
chapters.text: The principal bedroom takes its character from painted blossom panels set into ivory mouldings on both flank walls. A buttoned headboard, two armchairs at the window and a chocolate velvet bench at the foot of the bed complete it, the darkest note in an otherwise pale room.

chapters.title: The same care, away from the front.
chapters.text: Guest rooms and stairwells carry the identical vocabulary, ivory mouldings, herringbone oak, one ebonised piece, so nothing in the house reads as secondary.

chapters.title: Two rooms that change key.
chapters.text: The gym and garage are the only spaces to break the ivory palette, mirror, graphite and dark oak, treated as considered interiors rather than utility rooms.

chapters.title: One window, two storeys tall.
chapters.text: The rear elevation is organised around a single monumental arched window under a domed pediment, with carved friezes either side and a lap pool set into clipped lawn below. Loungers, a dining pergola and topiary complete the sequence from the reception out to the water.

name: Beach Mansion
tagline: Warm minimalism, at the waterline.
summary: A beachfront residence conceived as one continuous material envelope: full-height walnut and oak panelling, travertine floors, book-matched stone and bronze-tinted mirror, wrapped around glazing that opens to the marina skyline on two sides.
story: Colour discipline carries the whole apartment, bone, sand, walnut and brushed brass, with olive velvet as the single accent, appearing in the living room, both bedrooms and nowhere else.

chapters.title: Dark walnut, then light.
chapters.text: The foyer is deliberately the darkest room in the apartment, walnut on every plane, a single lit artwork, and a floating marble console that cantilevers past its pier. The travertine floor and the view straight through to the glazing do the rest.

chapters.title: One slab, wrapped.
chapters.text: The island is a single quartzite volume with mitred returns and brass toe details, facing an onyx backsplash flanked by lit brass shelving. Tall walnut units absorb the ovens and coffee machine so the working wall reads as panelling, not appliances.

name: Panorama Residence
tagline: Two apartments, one house.
summary: Two neighbouring apartments at Panorama were merged into a single residence: the party wall removed, circulation re-planned around one long living axis, and the whole envelope rebuilt in oak, travertine and plaster so no join reads anywhere.
story: The palette is a single family of sand and bone, with soft-green upholstery as the only accent. Curved plaster ceiling reveals, herringbone oak floors and round rugs carry the geometry from the entrance through to the bedrooms.

chapters.title: One long curve, one green chair.
chapters.text: A single curved sofa runs the length of the glazing on a round wool rug, faced by one olive velvet lounge chair, the only saturated colour on the floor. Oak joinery with open display bays lines the opposite wall and turns the corner into the dining room.

chapters.title: A stone pier, not a wall.
chapters.text: Where the two apartments meet, a rough-hewn stone pier washed from above marks the join and screens the formal sitting room from the dining table beyond. A reeded glass slider closes it off when needed without losing the light.

chapters.title: Ten seats, under the light well.
chapters.text: The dining table sits directly under the double-height clerestory left by the combination, with three sculptural fabric pendants filling the volume. Fully upholstered chairs and a fluted timber base keep the whole setting soft.

chapters.title: Calacatta, wall to island.
chapters.text: One slab of gold-veined calacatta runs from the splashback into the island's mitred waterfall, with bronze-glass display cabinets lit shelf by shelf above the counter. Everything else is flush oak, ovens and tall storage disappear into the panelling.

chapters.title: The bathroom, brought into the room.
chapters.text: Rather than hide it behind a corridor, the ensuite sits in the bedroom as a glazed travertine box with a freestanding tub and rain shower, framed in slim black steel. A circular ceiling cove and round rug centre the bed opposite it.

chapters.title: Joinery does all the work.
chapters.text: The dressing room and second bedroom are built entirely from millwork, bronze-glass fronts, lit interiors, upholstered panels, so both rooms hold everything without a single freestanding piece of storage.

chapters.title: Playful, still the same house.
chapters.text: The children's rooms take the adult vocabulary, fluted panels, arched niches, integrated light, and add one soft ochre and a cloud pendant, without breaking the palette.

chapters.title: Terracotta shade, city beyond.
chapters.text: A terracotta batten pergola on round columns shades a ten-seat table and an outdoor kitchen, throwing striped light across pale porcelain paving. Glass balustrades keep the skyline uninterrupted from seated height.

chapters.title: One round bed, facing out.
chapters.text: At the open end of the pergola a single round daybed sits against the glass, with planters and concealed strip light along the parapet. It is the only piece of furniture in that bay, the view does the rest.

name: Sky View Residence
tagline: Living above the skyline.
summary: Sky View Residence is a high-floor apartment in Downtown Dubai. Floor-to-ceiling glazing wraps the main living space, so the city's towers and the sunset become part of every room.
story: Inside, the palette is warm and quiet: travertine and black marble, rich walnut joinery, cream upholstery and bronze accents, all lit by concealed cove lighting that carries the glow of the evening sky indoors.

chapters.title: Travertine, walnut and space to gather.
chapters.text: A long travertine wall holds the media screen above a low walnut console, beside a lit glass-fronted bar cabinet. The dining table for ten sits on a soft rug across the room, with warm oak floors running through the whole space.

chapters.title: Black marble, bronze mirrors.
chapters.text: A black marble table on a brass frame seats ten on curved cream chairs. Two large bevelled bronze mirrors double the room and reflect a bold abstract artwork, with a walnut bar cabinet lit shelf by shelf beside it.

chapters.title: Waking up to the city.
chapters.text: A dark marble wall panel and a tall walnut pier frame an upholstered bed with a floating walnut bedside unit. Concealed lighting runs along the ceiling and the base of the stone, and the window opens straight onto the towers.

chapters.title: A spa bath in the sky.
chapters.text: Stone-clad walls and floors, a floating vanity with a black marble top and vessel basin, and black-framed glass enclosures for the rain shower and WC. A full-height window runs the length of the room, with the city far below.

name: Villa Orbis
tagline: Circles of light, on the water.
summary: Villa Orbis is a full renovation of a waterfront villa on Frond M, Palm Jumeirah. Its name comes from the circle that repeats through the home: a domed, cove-lit ceiling over the living room, floating ring pendants, and a sculpted spiral stair rising to a round lightwell.
story: The palette pairs book-matched white marble with bold black veining, warm walnut joinery and polished marble floors. Upstairs, every bedroom opens through frameless picture windows onto the lagoon, the Palm villas and the Dubai Marina skyline.

chapters.title: One long room, under floating rings.
chapters.text: The dining room and kitchen share a single open plan on polished marble floors. A marble table with brass edging sits beneath three floating ring pendants, framed by a marble and walnut media wall on one side and full-height sheers on the other.

chapters.title: Black, walnut and marble.
chapters.text: Full-height walnut and matt black cabinetry wrap a lit marble splashback with floating black shelves. A black marble waterfall island on a fluted walnut base seats three, with integrated ovens, a coffee station and a window over the sink.

chapters.title: A spiral to the light.
chapters.text: The stair is the heart of the villa: black steel balustrades sweep up through three levels to a round, cove-lit lightwell. Slim marble wall lights trace the climb, and narrow windows bring daylight down the void.

chapters.title: The lagoon, framed.
chapters.text: A single frameless picture window runs the width of the room, turning the lagoon, the Palm villas and the Marina skyline into the view from the bed.

chapters.title: Marble, walnut and calm.
chapters.text: A book-matched marble panel, lit at its edges, sits between walnut panels behind an upholstered bed with built-in side wings. Glass pendants hang at each side, and a walk-in wardrobe with lit glass-fronted shelving opens off the room.

chapters.title: Fluted stone, floating vanity.
chapters.text: A fluted marble wall frames two backlit mirrors and slim pendant lights. The double vanity is cut from solid marble and floats on a fluted walnut base with a lit shelf below, finished with black wall-mounted taps.

chapters.title: Two views, one room.
chapters.text: In the corner suite, a glazed balcony door and a wide picture window meet, giving the room two views of the water. A lounge chair by the glass and a marble and walnut headboard wall complete it.

chapters.title: Soft panels, city view.
chapters.text: A tall channelled headboard runs to the ceiling between lit marble panels, with floating walnut bedside units and slim pendants. The window frames the Marina skyline across the lagoon.

name: Oceana Pacific
tagline: Warm walnut, open to the city.
summary: A full renovation of an apartment in the Pacific building at Oceana, Palm Jumeirah. The brief was a calm, hotel-grade home: walnut joinery, soft stone, pale oak floors and warm concealed lighting throughout.
story: The living room opens through full-height glazing onto a terrace with palms and the Dubai skyline beyond. Every room is tied together by the same walnut and the same line of warm light, from the kitchen and study to the bedrooms and baths.

chapters.title: One open room, full of sun.
chapters.text: Living, dining and kitchen share one open plan. A deep cream sectional faces the glazing, a dark timber table sits under a slim linear pendant, and the terrace and pool are a step away.

chapters.title: Walnut and stone, made to gather.
chapters.text: A wall of full-height walnut hides the appliances, beside handleless cream cabinets and a stone splashback. The stone island has a lit underside, bar seating and an integrated wine fridge, facing a dining table for eight.

chapters.title: A library corner, lit from within.
chapters.text: Walnut shelving wraps the corner of the lounge, each shelf lit along its edge, around a built-in desk. Opposite, a cream panelled media wall with floating walnut shelves keeps the room quiet.

chapters.title: Soft, warm and quiet.
chapters.text: A walnut wall runs the length of the room, holding the TV, a floating vanity desk and lit storage. An upholstered headboard sits against a walnut band with a hidden light line, framed by layered sheers and blackout curtains.

chapters.title: Dark marble, bright detail.
chapters.text: A double vanity carved from dark green marble with bold white veining, with wall-mounted chrome taps and twin basins. A lit walnut niche sits between two mirrors, with soft light washing the stone walls on either side.

name: Villa Verdana
tagline: Green marble, soaring light.
summary: Villa Verdana is a family villa in Sienna Lakes, Jumeirah Golf Estates. Its name comes from the deep green marble at the heart of the home, a single book-matched slab rising the full height of the living hall.
story: Around it, the palette stays soft and warm: fluted stone cladding, ivory upholstery, olive velvet and brass. Full-height arched glazing pulls the garden in, while a floating sculpture of woven light ribbons fills the double-height volume.

chapters.title: Two storeys, one quiet wall.
chapters.text: A plastered media wall rises between two backlit columns of green marble, with floating display shelves and a long linear fire below. Oak library joinery and a glass-railed gallery frame the room on the other side.

chapters.title: A room planned from above.
chapters.text: Seen from the upper gallery, the layout reads clearly: a deep L-shaped sofa, nested marble tables and a single olive velvet armchair, all set on a textured rug and washed in sunlight from the glazing.

chapters.title: Golden hour, indoors.
chapters.text: In the late afternoon, sunlight pours through the arched glazing and across the fluted stone, catching the brass lamps and the veins of the marble. The garden and its mature trees become part of the room.

name: Villa 21, Sienna Lakes
tagline: Timeless luxury in the heart of Jumeirah Golf Estates.
summary: Villa 21 is a brand-new, fully renovated five-bedroom residence in the prestigious Sienna Lakes community, 7,808 sq ft of built-up area on a 7,673 sq ft plot, where every corner reflects meticulous craftsmanship.
story: Elevated to our turnkey standard through a complete structural and interior renovation, the home balances sophisticated modern comfort with the precision-engineered detail of studio-grade work, an enduring statement of privacy and elegance.

chapters.title: Living, on a double-height scale.
chapters.text: The main living volume rises through two storeys to a cascading glass-leaf pendant, anchored by a travertine media wall, oak herringbone floors and full-height glazing that floods the room with light.

chapters.title: A kitchen wrapped in book-matched stone.
chapters.text: Dark oak joinery frames an illuminated Calacatta Viola feature wall and a full suite of integrated Miele appliances. A sculpted stone island anchors the room, engineered for quiet family mornings and high-level entertaining alike.

chapters.title: Gather, under gold and glass.
chapters.text: A formal dining room crowned by a sculptural gold-leaf chandelier, opening through wide cased portals to the kitchen and lounge, sized for entertaining and held in the home's calm palette of stone and oak.

chapters.title: A sculpted staircase and a light-filled void.
chapters.text: The heart of the home is a piece of engineering and craft, a feature staircase in dark oak and blackened steel rising through a double-height hall, set against warm stone and a cloud of hand-blown glass.

chapters.title: Bathe with the lake in view.
chapters.text: A book-matched green-marble spa bath opens through full-height glazing onto the lake, a freestanding stone tub, twin vanities and rain showers in a serene, light-filled retreat.

chapters.title: A table made for gathering.
chapters.text: A sculpted marble dining table sits against a backlit stone-and-oak display wall with concealed wine storage, intimate enough for family, scaled for entertaining at the highest level.

chapters.title: Living, onto the green.
chapters.text: A sunken fire-pit lounge and built-in seating sit among mature planting, opening directly onto the fairway and lake, outdoor living against the full sweep of Jumeirah Golf Estates.

chapters.title: On the edge of the fairway.
chapters.text: A resort-grade lap pool and landscaped garden run straight out to the lake and golf course, the full sweep of Jumeirah Golf Estates as a private backdrop, from a clean contemporary façade.

name: One JBR Apartment
tagline: Lines of light, walnut and stone.
summary: One JBR Apartment is a high-floor residence in Jumeirah Beach Residence. A frame of dark walnut slats, threaded with fine lines of light, wraps the open living, dining and kitchen space and ties the whole plan together.
story: The palette is calm and tailored: white marble floors, dark marble in the kitchen and bedroom, a sculpted bar in walnut and backlit onyx, soft grey upholstery and globe pendants, with bathrooms that open onto the sea and the Palm.

chapters.title: One open plan, framed in walnut.
chapters.text: A deep grey modular sofa anchors the living room, with glass and stone side tables and a lit glass display cabinet. Dark walnut slats rise up the walls and run across the ceiling, each one carrying a fine line of light, so living, dining and kitchen read as a single, composed space.

chapters.title: Walnut and onyx, lit from within.
chapters.text: The bar is a sculpted, curving piece of joinery in book-matched walnut, set with batons of backlit onyx at staggered heights and topped in onyx. Behind it, grey wall panels with fine metal inlays and walnut insets form a quiet backdrop, under a linear globe pendant.

chapters.title: Dark marble, quiet white walls.
chapters.text: A waterfall island in dark veined marble faces full-height handleless cabinetry with an integrated wine store. Beyond it, a white gallery corridor with dark timber reveals leads to the private rooms, past a backlit oval mirror set into the walnut slat wall.

chapters.title: Dark wood, grey marble.
chapters.text: The master bedroom is calm and dark. Tall timber panels with slim metal inlays frame an upholstered bed, while a full-height slab of grey veined marble turns the corner toward the bathroom. Clusters of pendant bulbs replace bedside lamps, and heavy drapes close off the view.

chapters.title: A shower above the sea.
chapters.text: In the master bathroom, a walk-in shower lined in large-format stone ends at a full-height window, looking out over the water and the Palm. A recessed, lit niche in warm timber and a linear drain keep every surface clean and uninterrupted.

chapters.title: Soft light, warm stone.
chapters.text: Each bathroom has its own mood, built from the same few materials: textured stone, dark timber, smoked glass and brushed fittings, lit by globe sconces and backlit mirrors.

name: Regal Polyclinic
tagline: Clinical precision, hospitality calm.
summary: Regal Polyclinic in Business Bay exemplifies modern interior design and renovation excellence, a serene, sophisticated healthcare environment where the anxiety usually attached to a clinic visit simply falls away. A spacious, airy lobby in neutral tones, lifted by tasteful colour accents, sets the tone from the door.
story: High-quality materials, marble surfaces, wood accents and seamless white joinery, deliver durability and a premium feel under constant use, while state-of-the-art medical technology is integrated into the fabric of each room to support efficient clinical workflows.

chapters.title: First impression, first reassurance.
chapters.text: A tall, light-filled arrival hall reads more like a gallery than a waiting room. A solid-surface reception counter floats free of the walls, textured plaster and concealed cove light wash the brand wall, and a hand-bent ribbon pendant traces the ceiling above. Deep-blue modular seating and marble side tables carry the accent through the male and female lounges.

name: Villa Elara
tagline: A quiet, light-filled home on Frond E.
summary: Villa Elara is a contemporary family villa on Frond E of Palm Jumeirah. It's a soft, neutral home where grey marble, smoked oak joinery and black-framed glazing are set against pale walls and wide-plank oak floors, with the Dubai Marina skyline across the water.
story: Designed and, the home centres on an open entertaining level: an island bar with a hanging glass rack, a dining room under a lit oval cove, and a dark, tailored kitchen behind reeded-glass doors.

chapters.title: Gathered beneath a ring of light.
chapters.text: An oval oak table sits under a softly lit ceiling cove and sculptural wire pendants, with full-height glazing opening to the terrace and the skyline beyond.

chapters.title: An island bar, at the heart of the home.
chapters.text: A waterfall marble island with a fluted oak front and concealed lighting anchors the living level. A suspended black-steel rack holds glassware and bottles overhead, and full-height oak joinery wraps the wall with lit display shelving.

chapters.title: Darker, and quietly tailored.
chapters.text: Matte black tall units and oak upper cabinetry frame a stone-topped island, with black-framed reeded-glass doors letting light through from the rooms beyond.

name: Villa Imperiale
tagline: A symphony of opulence and modern architecture.
summary: Redefining the standard of Frond K, Villa Imperiale is a brand-new four-bedroom masterpiece by our team. Formerly a Central Rotunda villa, Villa 39, the residence was stripped to its soul and reimagined from the ground up to capture the definitive Palm Jumeirah lifestyle.
story: Set upon a sprawling 7,757 sq ft plot, one of the largest in the Garden Homes collection, the home transitions seamlessly from meticulously curated interiors to an outdoor sanctuary, an architectural sunken fire pit, a resort-style pool and a professional-grade BBQ lounge, designed for the art of entertaining.

chapters.title: Light, held in soaring arches.
chapters.text: The main living volume rises through double-height arched windows to sculptural pendant lights, a serene, ivory-toned room with a textured stone media wall and a curved modular sofa, opening directly onto the pool and beach beyond.

chapters.title: A kitchen in black marble and oak.
chapters.text: A dramatic kitchen pairs book-matched black marble with warm oak joinery, a sculptural island and a full suite of integrated appliances. A gloss dining table and gallery-scale artwork turn everyday dining into an occasion.

chapters.title: Wake to the skyline and the sea.
chapters.text: The principal suite opens through full-height glazing onto the lagoon and the Dubai Marina skyline, a sculptural upholstered bed, fluted feature wall and a connecting dressing room, calm and pared-back in warm neutral tones.

chapters.title: A wardrobe in smoked oak and glass.
chapters.text: The connecting dressing room is wrapped in smoked-oak joinery and bronze-tinted glass, with brushed-brass detailing and a full wall of glazing to the sea, a serene, hotel-grade space crafted entirely in-house.

chapters.title: An architectural sunken fire pit.
chapters.text: A resort-style pool meets an architectural sunken seating lounge with a linear fire pit, framed by the arched façade and concealed lighting, outdoor living engineered for the long Palm Jumeirah evenings.

chapters.title: Beachfront living, from dusk to dark.
chapters.text: The terrace runs straight to the sand, with the Dubai Marina skyline across the water, a sunken beach lounge and fire pit that move effortlessly from golden-hour gatherings to glowing evenings on the Palm.

chapters.title: A courtyard that glows after dark.
chapters.text: A sculpted water feature, manicured lawn and curated planting are threaded with colour-changing light and concealed LED, a private garden courtyard that turns the arrival sequence into theatre at night.

name: Villa Venetian
tagline: A Mediterranean shell, emptied of weight.
summary: Set on the water's edge in Jumeirah Islands, Villa Venetian keeps the tiled roofline and proportions of its neighbours, then strips the interior back to light, stone and air. A double-height glazed core opens the house to the lake; everything else recedes into off-white micro-cement and ribbons of dark timber.
story: Our team delivered the project end to end, structure, glazing, marble, joinery, lighting, automation and landscaping, tuning each room to a single, restrained palette so the water and the sunset do the decorating.

chapters.title: Two storeys of light.
chapters.text: The heart of the house is a double-height volume where a cascading porcelain-petal chandelier descends past a full-height window to the lake. A linear flame fireplace and a sculptural mirror anchor the dining table; the lounge sits a step away, all held in the same hushed, light-filled palette.

chapters.title: A quiet, dark-wrapped retreat.
chapters.text: A full-height fumed-timber headboard wall grounds the principal bedroom, set against pale floors and a soft grey rug. A tan leather daybed, a glazed dressing corner and a window to the garden keep the room generous and serene.

chapters.title: Black walls, white light.
chapters.text: Floor-to-ceiling matte-black joinery, lit on every shelf, lines a compact study that opens through a bay window to the pool. A pale desk and a pair of cane-and-ebony chairs keep the room sharp, considered and entirely bespoke.

chapters.title: From driveway to water's edge.
chapters.text: Outside, the house is staged for dusk, a lit, illuminated-stone pool and sunken lounge facing the Dubai skyline, and an arrival court where uplit palms and rose beds frame the floodlit façade.
